sanjay: Quick heads up — I ran the adaptive-token-budget canary run against a 2h window (us-east canary traffic). Sharing raw notes.
olivia: Awesome, curious about p95 and kv behavior. :eyes:
mike: Is this the run that switches kernel selection heuristics too?
sanjay: Yes — we enabled kernel-selection: seq<=64 -> pad-optim int8 kernel, otherwise default. Also flipped admit.mode -> dynamic_token_budget and set a modest burst ratio.
perf-bot: [metric snapshot] p50=78ms p95=310ms p99=780ms kv_hit_rate=27% tokens_per_req=120 avg_batch=7
lisa: p95 jumped from 275ms -> 310ms? throughput change?
sanjay: Throughput improved ~+7% aggregate QPS under same traffic. But we saw more variance on p95 due to occasional tail queuing when token-budget depleted.
olivia: Do we have the config used? want to reproduce locally.
sanjay: Pasting minimal config we used:
```
admit:
  mode: dynamic_token_budget
  base_target_tokens: 4096
  burst_token_ratio: 1.5
  token_replenish_ms: 250
  kv_priority: prefix
  soft_429: true
kernel_selection:
  short_seq_threshold: 64
  short_seq_kernel: int8_pad_opt
  fallback_kernel: default
batching:
  max_batch_size: 32
  target_batch_time_ms: 8
```
mike: Interesting. So token_replenish_ms is 250 — that's pretty aggressive. Could cause short bursts then a quiet window.
sanjay: Exactly. We saw admission behaviour like: quick bursts fill budget, then soft 429s for ~200-600ms until replenish. Logs showed admit decisions correlated with token_budget < 0.
perf-bot: [trace] trace_id=tr-9ab: admit=soft_reject reason=token_budget low_kv_hits=0.12 batch_formed=3
lisa: KV cache help — hit rate went from ~18% baseline -> 27% with prefix caching, which explains throughput up but not p95.
olivia: Any perf regressions linked to kernel change? maybe int8_pad_opt has worse cold-path for longer sequences.
sanjay: We profiled top 1% tails: many tails were requests that got assigned to fallback kernel mid-inference due to padding mismatch, causing an extra copy path. We should tighten kernel-selection invariants.
mike: Could we make kernel choice sticky per request (once assigned) to avoid mid-inference fallback?
sanjay: We tried sticky assignment in a small A/B — reduced p95 tails by ~40% for affected requests. But it slightly increased average memory footprint.
lisa: Tradeoff seems acceptable for customer SLAs. Any rollback criteria?
olivia: If p95 > 350ms or soft_429 rate > 1% for 15m, rollback. Also alert when kv_hit_rate drops > 5% vs baseline.
sanjay: Agreed. Next steps:
- roll kernel sticky change to canary and re-run dynamic_token_budget with token_replenish_ms=500 (smoother)
- instrument more detailed admit traces (include token_budget before/after)
- run synthetic workload with seq mix skewed to short/long to validate kernel path
mike: I'll own the canary rollout tonight and hook up trace logs to perf-dash.
lisa: I'll draft a PR to make kernel assignment sticky behind a flag and add the rollback alarms.
olivia: Thanks team. Keep notes short in this thread and ping if you need help with infra keys. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [action] canary_run_started id=canary-181234-a
sanjay: I'll post final numbers in ~3h.
